key_insight: An operation-aware multimodal model combining patient data, clinical notes, and hospital workload achieved the strongest ICU readmission prediction among the evaluated approaches.
clinical_relevance: Incorporating operational context may help discharge-risk tools reflect both patient condition and hospital pressures, but clinical benefit remains unproven.
method: Combined workload and admission-flow indicators with vital signs, ICD/DRG codes, and clinical notes.
Used multi-agent extraction and self-evolving retrieval-augmented generation to remove note-template noise.
Applied end-to-end Transformer fine-tuning, class reweighting, and decision-threshold calibration.
evidence_signal: Across 20 independent runs on 20,000 MIMIC-III ICU stays with approximately 10.5% readmissions, the best model achieved AUROC 0.8288 ± 0.0110, PR-AUC 0.4373 ± 0.0310, and F1 0.4757 ± 0.0196.
watch_item: The abstract reports no external or prospective validation; performance and alert burden in other hospitals remain uncertain.
paper_title: Operation-aware Multimodal Clinical Decision Support System for ICU Discharge Risk Assessment
